# Writing a frontend

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the code and docs/api/groups.toml. Do not edit. -->

A frontend holds a `Client`, in this process or over the wire, and reads the line a person typed.

Names: `Client`, `CommandFailed`, `Completion`, `ImageInput`, `LocalClient`, `MAX_INPUT_BYTES`, `MAX_INPUT_IMAGES`, `Parsed`, `RemoteClient`, `UnknownCommand`, `commandline.Completion`, `commandline.STDIN`, `commandline.completions`, `commandline.parse`, `commandline.value`, `commandline.values`

## Client

```python
class Client(AsyncIterator[Event], Protocol)
    id: str
```

What a frontend holds. Iterating it yields the events: first a snapshot (`Commands`, a
`CursorView` per open cursor, a `CursorGone` per closed one, then `Labels`), then changes as
they happen, until the driver stops (the stream ends), or the driver fails or the client is
`CutOff` for falling behind (it raises `ConnectionError`). Every call raises `ConnectionError`
once the driver has failed or stopped, or the client has been closed or cut off.

### Client.input

```python
async def input(self, cursor: int, text: str, images: Sequence[ImageInput] = ()) -> int
```

Add `text` to the cursor's scratchpad as this client's input, with `images` after it
(D31); returns the item. At most `MAX_INPUT_IMAGES` images, each an `ImageInput` (its
bytes are checked as it is made: `BadImage`). The images are held to the model of the
cursor's branch as a tool's are (D30 section 6): `ValueError` saying why if it does not
take images or one is over its provider's limits, `MissingImage` for a `sha256` the
session does not hold, `ValueError` for too many; nothing is added then.

### Client.send

```python
async def send(self, cursor: int, text: str, images: Sequence[ImageInput] = ()) -> int
```

`input` with auto-step on.

### Client.step

```python
async def step(self, cursor: int) -> None
```

Start a step on a cursor at rest; `Busy` otherwise.

### Client.go_to

```python
async def go_to(self, cursor: int, to: int) -> None
```

Move the cursor to node `to`, aborting a busy step (which declines its open
questions).

### Client.remove_item

```python
async def remove_item(self, cursor: int, item: int) -> None
```

Take back a pending input this client added to `cursor` (`input` or `send`): it is
removed from the scratchpad before the cursor delivers it. `LookupError` once it is
delivered, or if there is no such item on the cursor; `PermissionError` for an item
another client or an extension added. Wakes nothing and does not turn auto-step off.

### Client.set_auto

```python
async def set_auto(self, cursor: int, on: bool) -> None
```

Turn `cursor`'s auto-step on or off; on wakes it.

### Client.abort

```python
async def abort(self, cursor: int) -> None
```

Abort the cursor's step and decline its open questions.

### Client.open

```python
async def open(self, at: int) -> int
```

Open a cursor at node `at`; it wakes. Returns its id.

### Client.close_cursor

```python
async def close_cursor(self, cursor: int) -> None
```

Close the cursor (D17): abort its step as `abort` does, wait for it to rest, drop its
pending items, and close it. Clients are sent a `CursorGone`. Its id, last node and
labels stay; `reopen` restarts from them. `CursorClosed` if it is already closed.

### Client.reopen

```python
async def reopen(self, cursor: int) -> int
```

Open a new cursor at the closed `cursor`'s last node, and move each of its labels
onto it. Returns the new id. `ValueError` if `cursor` is open, `NoSuchCursor` if it was
never opened.

### Client.set_label

```python
async def set_label(self, cursor: int, label: str) -> None
```

Put `label` on `cursor`; a label set elsewhere moves.

### Client.remove_label

```python
async def remove_label(self, label: str) -> None
```

Remove `label`; `NoSuchLabel` if there is none.

### Client.watch

```python
async def watch(self, cursors: Collection[int]) -> None
```

Hear the `Live` of exactly these cursors from now on (a call replaces the last),
starting with what each sample in flight has streamed that is not in the tree yet.

### Client.answer

```python
async def answer(self, question: int, value: object) -> None
```

Answer an open question with a decoded JSON value; `None` declines. `ValueError` if
the value is wrong (the question stays open), `LookupError` if the question is closed
or unknown (the first good answer wins), `PermissionError` if it is for another
client.

### Client.close

```python
async def close(self) -> None
```

Disconnect: the stream ends and the client is no longer connected.

### Client.node

```python
async def node(self, id: int) -> Node
```

The node with this id; `NoSuchNode` if there is none.

### Client.nodes

```python
async def nodes(self, start: int, limit: int) -> list[Node]
```

Up to `limit` nodes from id `start`, in id order; none past the end. Ids are dense
and a node never changes, so a tree is read in ranges. `ValueError` for a negative
`start` or `limit`.

### Client.walk

```python
async def walk(self, id: int) -> list[Node]
```

The nodes from the root to `id`.

### Client.children

```python
async def children(self, id: int) -> list[int]
```

The ids of the children of node `id`, in append order.

### Client.image

```python
async def image(self, sha256: str) -> str
```

The bytes of the image named `sha256` that this session holds (a node's, or an input's
on a scratchpad), as base64: what a client draws a node's `Image` with (D31).
`MissingImage` (a `LookupError`) if the session holds none by that name.

### Client.commands

```python
async def commands(self) -> tuple[Form, ...]
```

Each command's form: its name, description and argument schema (named types with
their `"format"`, each default). If some extension has options there is one more,
`config`, whose one argument is the extension; it is changed with `configure`, not `run`.
A client with a stream need not call it: the stream opens with them in `Commands`, and
sends them again whenever they change.

### Client.run

```python
async def run(self, cursor: int, command: str, args: Mapping[str, object]) -> str | None
```

Run `/command` (`"note"`, or `"a:note"`, the extension's qualified name) with decoded
JSON `args` on `cursor`; returns the command's result
(`None` if it has none) once it has finished. `CommandFailed` (its message is the
failure as `"Type: msg"`) if it raised, or was aborted; it is raised as soon as the
command raises, even when the command's step has not yet ended: the cursor may still be
busy for a moment while the step ends, and a retry then gets `Busy`. A command's `progress`
and `cursor.tell` arrive as `Notice`s. `LookupError` for an unknown command or a bare name
two extensions share (`"/note is two commands: /a:note, /b:note"`), `ValueError`
naming the problem for arguments that fit no parameter (the values are checked with the
session, `"new"` last), `Busy` for a command that runs as a step of the cursor when it is
not at rest.

### Client.options

```python
async def options(self, cursor: int, extension: str) -> Form
```

`extension`'s options as they stand at `cursor`: a form whose schema has every
option, each default the value now. `ConfigError` if it has no options.

### Client.configure

```python
async def configure(
    self,
    cursor: int,
    extension: str,
    values: Mapping[str, object],
    *,
    save: bool = False,
) -> None
```

Change the options named in `values` (decoded JSON) of `extension` on `cursor`'s
branch: a step of the cursor writes a `Config` node. With `save`, the server also writes the
user's config file (`extensions.<name>`), which every session reads: the options in `values`
and those a `Config` node on the branch set, wherever they differ from the file's (options
equal to the file's stay untouched; `values` may be `{}`; options only the user, project
or command-line layers set are not copied). A client needs no access to that file.
`ConfigError`
for an extension without options, or values its options type refuses (or, with `save`,
a driver with no user config), `Busy` unless the cursor is at rest; nothing is written
then, neither node nor file.

### Client.complete

```python
async def complete(self, cursor: int, named: str, prefix: str) -> list[Completion]
```

The values of a named type (`"path"`, `"model"`, `"cursor"`, `"label"`, `"node"`;
the `"format"` of a schema) that start with `prefix`, as `cursor` sees them, each a
`Completion`: the `value`, and the `label` and `detail` a list shows (D32 section 1).
Paths are the driver's machine's, relative to its working directory.

### Client.parse_line

```python
async def parse_line(self, cursor: int, line: str) -> Parsed
```

`commandline.parse` of `line` with this driver's forms and the options forms
`cursor` sees: the command, its arguments, and the required parameters still `missing`.
`UnknownCommand` if no command has the name (send the line as text), `ValueError` for a
line that cannot be read, plain `LookupError` for a bare name two extensions share.

### Client.complete_line

```python
async def complete_line(self, cursor: int, line: str) -> list[Completion]
```

`commandline.completions` of `line` on the driver: what could finish its last
word, in one call, as `Completion`s.

## CommandFailed

```python
class CommandFailed(RuntimeError)
```

A command raised, or returned what is not a `str` or `None`. The message is the failure
as `"Type: msg"`. `Client.run` raises it as soon as the command raises; an aborted one raises
it too. A command raises it itself to refuse (its arguments, say), with a message for the
person: the caller gets that message as written, with no traceback, and a command that takes
a `Cursor` does not fail its step for it.

## Completion

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Completion
    value: str
    label: str | None = None
    detail: str | None = None
```

One thing that could finish what is being typed (D32 section 1). `value` is what is
inserted, or sent: it replaces the word being typed whole (quoted for a command line, unquoted
from `Client.complete` and `values`). `label` is what a list shows instead of `value` (`None`:
show `value`), and `detail` one line beside it, dimmed (`None`: nothing). Neither holds a
newline (whitespace runs become one space), and `detail` is cut at `DETAIL_WIDTH` characters
with `…`.

## ImageInput

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ImageInput
    data: str | None = None
    sha256: str | None = None
```

One image a client sends with an input (D31): exactly one of `data`, the image file's bytes
in standard base64 (with padding, nothing else), or `sha256`, the name of an image this
session already keeps (a node's or an input's; nothing is read from a path). The format and
size are read from the bytes, never taken from the client. Built from the wire or by hand,
it is checked at once: `BadImage` (a `ValueError`) for bytes that are not strict base64 of
a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image of at most `MAX_INPUT_BYTES`, or a `sha256` that is not 64
lowercase hex digits. Its `repr` never shows the bytes.

### ImageInput.of

```python
@classmethod
def of(cls, data: bytes) -> Self
```

The input of the image file `data`: its bytes as base64.

### ImageInput.image

```python
def image(self) -> Image | None
```

The image `data` holds, with its bytes; `None` for a `sha256`, which the session
resolves. `BadImage` as at construction.

## LocalClient

```python
class LocalClient(Client)
```

A `Client` in the driver's process, made by `Driver.client`: its stream opens with the
snapshot, in one act on the loop, so make it inside the running loop. Each call is
documented on `Client`.


The events the stream holds now, removed, without waiting. A server writes a
client's events as batches and sends each response after the events its call caused.

## MAX_INPUT_BYTES

```python
MAX_INPUT_BYTES: Final = 20 * MIB
```

The most bytes one image of an input may be, before base64 (D31; fixed for 0.18).

## MAX_INPUT_IMAGES

```python
MAX_INPUT_IMAGES: Final = 20
```

The most images one input may carry (D31; fixed for 0.18).

## Parsed

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Parsed
    command: Form
    args: dict[str, object]
    missing: tuple[str, ...]
    extension: str | None = None
    save: bool = False
```

A command line, read: the `command` form, its `args` (decoded JSON), and the `missing`
required parameters, in order, which a frontend asks for. For `/config <extension>` the
`command` is the extension's options form, `args` the options to change and `extension`
its name; with no `args` the line asks for the form, which a frontend shows from
`Client.options`. `save` is whether `--save` was typed. `run` makes the call.

### Parsed.run

```python
async def run(self, client: 'Client', cursor: int) -> str | None
```

`client.run` the command, or `client.configure` the extension's options; returns the
command's result.

## RemoteClient

```python
class RemoteClient(Client)
    welcome: Welcome
```

A `Client` of a session served by `tau serve`: build one with `RemoteClient.connect`. Each
call is documented once, on `Client`. It is also an async context manager that closes.

### RemoteClient.connect

```python
@classmethod
async def connect(cls, socket: str | PathLike[str], client: str, *, buffer: int = 256) -> Self
```

Dial the server at `socket` as `client` with an event stream of `buffer`, and say
`hello`. The snapshot is queued before this returns. `ProtocolMismatch` if the server
speaks another protocol, `OSError` if nothing answers at `socket` (or, on Windows,
always: see `require_unix_sockets`).

### RemoteClient.connect_http

```python
@classmethod
async def connect_http(cls, url: str, token: str, client: str, *, buffer: int = 256) -> Self
```

`connect`, to the HTTP edge at `url` (`http://HOST:PORT/`) with its bearer `token`.
`ConnectionRefusedError` if nothing listens there, `PermissionError` if the edge refuses
the token or this client's origin.

### RemoteClient.__aiter__

```python
def __aiter__(self) -> Self
```

### RemoteClient.__anext__

```python
async def __anext__(self) -> Event
```

### RemoteClient.__aenter__

```python
async def __aenter__(self) -> Self
```

### RemoteClient.__aexit__

```python
async def __aexit__(self, *exc: object) -> None
```

### RemoteClient.request

```python
async def request(self, method: str, params: Json) -> object
```

Send request `method` and wait for its result, decoded. `ConnectionError` if the
stream has ended; the exception the error code names if the server answered with
one.

### RemoteClient.call

```python
async def call(self, method: str, **args: object) -> object
```

`request` for a call's arguments: they are encoded by the call's signature, so a
value that is not JSON is a `TypeError` here, before anything is sent.

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Completion
    value: str
    label: str | None = None
    detail: str | None = None
```

One thing that could finish what is being typed (D32 section 1). `value` is what is
inserted, or sent: it replaces the word being typed whole (quoted for a command line, unquoted
from `Client.complete` and `values`). `label` is what a list shows instead of `value` (`None`:
show `value`), and `detail` one line beside it, dimmed (`None`: nothing). Neither holds a

## tau.commandline.STDIN

```python
STDIN = 'stdin'
```

A command parameter of this name is never read from the line: `tau -p` fills it with
standard input.

## tau.commandline.completions

```python
async def completions(
    line: str,
    commands: Sequence[Form],
    client: 'Client',
    cursor: int,
    options: Mapping[str, Form] = MappingProxyType({}),
) -> list[Completion]
```

What could finish the word being typed at the end of `line`, each a `Completion` whose
`value` is a whole word to replace it with (quoted if it needs to be, `name=` before it when
typed so): command names after `/` (detailed with the first line of the description and the
extension), then for each parameter its `values` (labelled with the item's label, else the
unquoted value); after `/config <extension>`, the extension's options (`--save` is typed, not
completed). Nothing for a line that is not a command line, an unknown command, or a word
past the last parameter.

## tau.commandline.parse

```python
def parse(
    line: str,
    commands: Sequence[Form],
    options: Mapping[str, Form] = MappingProxyType({}),
) -> Parsed
```

Read a line that starts with `/`. `UnknownCommand` if no command has the name, plain
`LookupError` ("/note is two commands: /a:note, /b:note") if a bare name is several
extensions' commands, `ValueError` naming the problem for a line that is not a command
line, quotes that do not close, too many words, a word that cannot be the parameter's
value, or `/config` of an extension not in `options` (the options forms of
`Client.options`, by extension).

## tau.commandline.value

```python
def value(text: str, schema: Json) -> object
```

The decoded JSON `text` stands for under `schema`: a command's argument, or the answer
to a question. `ValueError` if it stands for none.

## tau.commandline.values

```python
async def values(schema: Json, prefix: str, client: 'Client', cursor: int) -> list[Completion]
```

What could finish `prefix` as a value of `schema`, each a `Completion` whose `value` is a
whole value to replace it with (unquoted): a named type's through `client.complete` (paths on
the driver's machine), the values of a `Literal`, `true` and `false` (these three bare), the
items of a list after its last comma (`value` the whole list text, `label` the item's own, so
a list shows the items and not the growing text). Duplicates go by `value`, first kept.
